title: Regional fleet priority lanes and stable failover safeguards
creator: Liu Chen
description: Design and implement a priority-lane orchestration layer for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets. The feature provides configurable throughput lanes (reserved/soft/best-effort) per tenant and region, deterministic failover ordering across zones/regions, and residency-aware placement predicates so customer data never crosses forbidden geographies during normal operation or failover.
background: Current Dedicated fleets route by simple region affinity with naive fallback to any available capacity. Several customers requested: 1) per-tenant throughput guarantees across zones, 2) controlled soft fallbacks that preserve residency constraints, and 3) predictable failover ordering to avoid sudden global traffic shifts. We also observed a P1 incident (INC-2025-03-01) where an emergency cross-region failover caused transient egress violations for an EU-regulated tenant.
goals: (1) Expose lane types: reserved, soft-reserved (preemptible with warm-up), and best-effort; (2) Ensure failover follows an ordered policy respecting residency predicates and minimizing cross-region egress; (3) Implement graceful cache warming and staged traffic ramps to limit quality regressions; (4) Provide tooling in Console to visualize lane utilization and failover plans.
non_goals: We will not implement per-request latency SLAs in this phase or integrate with customer-side routing (BGP) — those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tenant can configure per-region lane quotas via API or Console. 2) On a simulated zone failure, traffic is moved according to the configured ordering and residency constraints with no residency-violating egress allowed. 3) Metrics for lane utilization, failover time, and cold-start regression are visible in Console. 4) System supports both Dedicated and Dedicated-hybrid fleets.
design_notes: - Placement predicate language: allow tags like region==eu && residency==eu-only. - Failover scoring: compute candidate targets by (residency_score, lane_capacity_left, latency_headroom). - Soft-reserved lane warm-up: maintain a small standing KV cache shadow so warm-up reduces first-token regressions. - Circuit-breaker: failover escalation uses exponential backoff and a cooldown window to avoid oscillation.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: Reserved lanes reduce available shared capacity and may increase cost; soft-reserved lanes complicate autoscaler heuristics. Risks: Complex placement predicates could increase scheduling latency; incorrect residency enforcement could cause compliance violations. Mitigations: conservative defaults, e2e residency tests, pre-deployment policy verification.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): API schema (lane types, quotas, residency predicates), scheduler hooks to reserve capacity slices per-lane, basic Console UI. Phase 2 (2 sprints): Failover coordinator implementing ordered escalation, warm-up mechanisms, and monitoring hooks. Phase 3: rollout, chaos testing, and perf tuning.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha on staging with synthetic tenants. 2) Invite pro-bono customers for beta on Dedicated-dev regions. 3) Graduated rollout by tenant size with feature flags, defaulting to soft-reserved off. 4) Monitor SLIs for 72h before expanding.
testing_plan: Unit tests for placement predicate parser, integration tests for ordered failover, residency gating tests that assert no cross-region egress, e2e chaos tests that simulate zone flaps and validate traffic ramps and KV cache warmup behavior.
observability_notes: Emit events: LaneAllocated, LanePreempt, FailoverPlanned, FailoverExecuted, ResidencyBlock. Tag traces with tenant_id, lane_id, source_zone, target_zone.
deploy_steps: 1) Merge feature branch behind flag. 2) Deploy scheduler changes to staging. 3) Enable feature for internal tenants. 4) Gradually flip flags for external tenants.
decisions: 1) Use lane-first allocation: reserved -> soft-reserved -> best-effort. 2) Failover uses ordered candidate list derived from residency score, not lowest-latency-first (to avoid unintentional egress). 3) Default soft-reserved warm-up size = 1% of tenant peak KV-cache footprint.
open_questions: 1) Should billing reflect on-demand fallback usage for reserved lanes? 2) How to expose lane preemption notifications to customers in webhooks?
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Initial design review with PM and Console. Feedback: add visual preview of failover path in Console (Grace).
2025-02-22: Scheduler prototype accepts lane quotas; basic predicate parser implemented (ENG-branch: feature/priority-lanes).
2025-02-28: Incident review incorporated — added explicit residency test harness and egress gate for EU tenants.
2025-03-05: Failover coordinator spec ready; beginning integration work with autoscaler team.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on predicate expressiveness, failure modes (oscillation), and billing implications. Confirm residency gating meets legal team's checklist.
next_actions: 1) Finalize API shape this week. 2) Schedule 60-minute joint working session with autoscaler owners. 3) Add e2e residency test to CI.
customer_communication: Draft targeted beta email and Console announcement templates in Drive (link in design_doc).
estimated_cost_impact: Medium; reserved lanes increase committed GPU fraction per-region and may raise unit costs for shared tenants.
regulatory_notes: Residency predicates must map to KMS and audit controls; ensure logs do not contain cross-region payloads. Security reviewed the initial spec on 2025-02-20.
approval_status: Design approved by Infra and Security on 2025-02-25
final_comment: This ticket ties into Dedicated V2 roadmap. Keep communications tight with Sales for customers with strict residency needs.
